New 18-assertion smoke proves kill/fast-pass/default-arming/process-group-reap.
usage: Run 'lattice validate'. A hung validate command now fails loud (exit 124, attributed to that command) at its per-command ceiling instead of the cli-engine ~300s global idle watchdog silently force-exiting the whole suite. Override per command via lattice.config.json validate.commands[].timeoutMs.
expectedOutcome: lattice validate passes all 6 commands; a hung command is killed at its ceiling with code 124 and timedOut=true in roughly timeoutMs wall-clock, not left to the 300s global watchdog.
actualTranscript: lattice validate -> 6/6 green (incl. validate-command-timeout smoke: 18 assertions). Live demo-hung {code:124,timedOut:true,wallMs:550} at timeoutMs=500; default-arming {code:124,timedOut:true} with no explicit timeoutMs; resolveMainRepoRoot(os.tmpdir()) returns the tmp path (isolated:true). validate --story coverage 6/6, missingRequired=0.
outcomeDiff: None — actual matches expected on every point.
limitations: Windows process-tree kill uses taskkill /t /f (best-effort, guarded against an unhandled-error crash; not runtime-exercised on this darwin host). POSIX process-group path fully exercised. Otherwise none — fully covered.
pitfalls: Genuine dual-host review was essential: Codex (host 2) round-1 caught the process-group MAJOR (direct-child-only kill let npm/sh grandchildren survive and hang 'close'); Claude caught the win32 124-contract MAJOR and the taskkill unhandled-error crash (F-001). 4 review rounds to converge. Tooling: perl 'alarm' does NOT survive exec() on macOS, so wrap 'codex exec' in perl fork+alarm (or the Bash timeout) to actually bound it; never pipe codex through '| tail' (buffers until EOF, hides progress/hangs). Evidence freshness drifts after every metadata commit — re-bind + 'validate --story' right before DONE.
